svg.aria-label: The Seven Checks and What Each One Owns showing the review areas from untrusted content through supply chain, with the failure each catches
svg.title: The Seven Checks and What Each One Owns
svg.text: The Seven Checks and What Each One Owns
Each owns one failure. One change to the configuration should light up exactly one check.
1. untrusted_content_boundary
Retrieved text concatenated with instructions.
A document can then issue instructions.
2. output_handling
Model output rendered unescaped, or executed.
Untrusted input from a very fluent source.
3. tool_permissions
Write or delete scope, unconfirmed.
Authority the task did not need.
4. spend_bounds
No cap per request or per user.
An availability risk, not a billing one.
5. secret_handling
Credentials in the image or the repository.
Both are distributable; history is forever.
6. data_retention
Traces unbounded, undeletable, unredacted.
Your most sensitive store.
7. dependency_pinning
Mutable image tag, unlocked dependencies.
Someone else can change what you deploy.
Why these seven compose into something worse
Each decision is defensible alone. Together: a retrieved document
issues instructions, the agent acts on them destructively, the output
renders unescaped, nothing caps the resulting loop, and the whole
exchange is logged permanently.
Prompt injection has no complete fix — instructions and data share one channel by construction.
Which is why the mitigation is the PERMISSION MODEL rather than the prompt: mark untrusted content, grant minimal
authority, confirm consequential actions, and assume the model may be persuaded.
